title: Private DR: expose backup windows, timeouts, and retry policies via values.yaml
author: Connor O'Brien
description: Context: Following PRs #433 (CronJobs/Jobs for scheduled backup + one-shot restore) and #447 (PDB + concurrency safeguards), operators asked for more control over when backups run and how aggressive retries/timeouts should be, especially in constrained VPCs and on-prem clusters where object storage can throttle. This PR exposes backup window scheduling, per-job timeouts, and retry/backoff policies as supported values.yaml knobs for the `redwood-private` chart, with safe defaults that match our current behavior. Changes: (1) Add `.Values.privateDr.backup.schedule` and optional `.Values.privateDr.backup.window` guidance so operators can align backups to low-traffic windows; (2) Expose `activeDeadlineSeconds`, `startingDeadlineSeconds`, and `successfulJobsHistoryLimit/failedJobsHistoryLimit` for the CronJob; (3) Expose `backoffLimit` + `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for backup/restore Jobs; (4) Plumb these values into templates for both scheduled backups and ad-hoc restore jobs; (5) Add values.yaml examples and upgrade notes (chart users on <=0.18.x need to re-run `helm diff` because defaults moved from hardcoded template values to values.yaml). Notes: This is intentionally not adding “pause backups” semantics; concurrency remains governed by `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` and the lock behavior introduced in #447. Testing: rendered templates validated via chart-testing; smoke install on kind; verified CronJob spec matches expected fields; verified overrides generate deterministic manifests. Follow-ups: docs PR will cross-link these options in the operator runbooks and recommend defaults by RPO/RTO tier.
commits: helm(private-dr): add values for backup schedule/window knobs
helm(private-dr): expose timeouts/deadlines for backup/restore jobs
helm(private-dr): expose retry/backoff + TTL for finished jobs
docs(values): add examples + upgrade notes for config surface
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Can we expose `activeDeadlineSeconds`? We had a drill where the backup ran long and the operator didn’t realize it would keep retrying for hours. Also want a clear place to set backoffLimit. Connor O'Brien (author): Yep — added `privateDr.backup.job.activeDeadlineSeconds` and `privateDr.backup.job.backoffLimit` with defaults matching current behavior; also added `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` so clusters don’t accumulate old Job objects during frequent backup schedules. Allison Grant (review): Please ensure we emit metrics even when jobs are killed by deadlines; but for the chart side, can we at least document how the timeout interacts with alerts? Connor O'Brien: Added a note in README upgrade section: alerts key off last successful backup age, so too-short deadlines can cause noisy failures; operator should tune deadline based on snapshot size and storage throughput. Diego Santos (review): We should keep templates backward compatible — if values are unset, don’t render fields so K8s defaults apply. Current diff renders `0` in one place. Connor O'Brien: Fixed: use `with` blocks and only render when value is non-empty; also normalized under `privateDr.backup.cronjob.*` vs `privateDr.backup.job.*` to avoid confusion. Marcus Lin (review): Any security implications? Ensure retry behavior doesn’t lead to credential logging or repeated auth failures. Connor O'Brien: No credential changes; templates do not print secret values. Added a short note encouraging least-privilege IAM and to treat repeated AccessDenied as misconfig (link to SRE runbook will live in docs repo). Rafael Mendes (final): Looks good. Please add one concrete example for “nightly backups with 2h deadline + 5 retries” in values.yaml comments. Connor O'Brien: Added example snippet and confirmed chart-testing passes. Approved + merged.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main on 2025-11-26 by Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Helm: `redwood-private` now supports configuring backup windows/schedules, job timeouts/deadlines, and retry/backoff policies via values.yaml. Upgrade note: previously hardcoded CronJob/Job defaults were moved into values; verify rendered manifests after upgrading if you had custom overlays.
